adjudication_label: mechanisms of grain size evolution under dual-beam vs helium
canonical_question: How do helium implantation and dual-beam (heavy ion) irradiation differentially drive grain size evolution in W-Ta-Cr-V-Hf refractory high-entropy alloys at 1173 K, specifically regarding the competition between grain growth and cascade-induced fragmentation?

question_variants.question: How does the 'grain growth' from He implantation at high temperatures compete with the 'grain refinement' from heavy ions at the same temperature?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The text states that He implantation causes grain growth, whereas dual-beam irradiation (He + heavy ions) leads to grain refinement. The competition is resolved by the presence of heavy ions causing overlapping cascades that fragment the grain structure, overriding the growth effect seen with He alone.

answers.answer: He implantation causes grain growth, while dual-beam irradiation leads to grain refinement and fragmentation. The refinement is attributed to overlapping cascades larger than the grain size creating stacking faults.
answers.measurement_outcome: grain refinement and fragmentation observed; no defect loops formed
answers.mechanism: Grain refinement caused by overlapping cascades larger than grain size creating stacking faults and fragmentation; He implantation alone causes grain growth.
answers.boundary_limitation: Hardness increase attributed to multiple synergistic processes.
evidence_spans: The results here demonstrate that grain refinement only occurred when the heavy ions are introduced.
This suggests that such a grain refinement observed in the dual-beam irradiation case was caused by a cascade effect.
The in situ nature of the experiments performed in this work has allowed us to observe the grain refinement effect in real-time

source_evidence_spans: As He implantation only causes grain growth and dual-beam irradiation leads to grain refinement

question_variants.question: What specific 'dual-beam ion irradiation' procedure caused the observed 'grain refinement' while 'He implantation' caused the 10 nm increase?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The text states that grain refinement occurred under dual-beam ion irradiation and that this was caused by a 'cascade effect' (overlapping cascades), while He implantation alone caused grain growth (10 nm increase). Specific procedural parameters (e.g., beam energies, flux ratios) for the dual-beam causing refinement are not fully detailed in the spans.

answers.answer: Grain refinement was observed 'when the heavy ions are introduced' in the dual-beam case, suggesting it was 'caused by a cascade effect'. The text notes the in situ nature allowed real-time observation. The 10 nm increase is associated with He implantation (see other evidence), while refinement is specific to the heavy ion/dual-beam case.

question_variants.question: How does the '10 nm increase' during He implantation relate to the 'grain-size' stability mentioned in point (4)?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The text describes the alloy having a 'thermally stable grain-size (with 10 nm increase during He implantation... and grain refinement under dual-beam ion irradiation)'. The relationship is that the 10 nm increase is a specific outcome of He implantation, while the overall stability is maintained despite this increase, contrasting with the refinement seen in dual-beam irradiation.

answers.answer: The study reports a 'thermally stable grain-size (with 10 nm increase during He implantation up to 8.45% and grain refinement under dual-beam ion irradiation)'. The 10 nm increase is a localized effect of He implantation, whereas the alloy maintains thermal stability, unlike the refinement driven by heavy ions.
answers.mechanism: Thermal stability with resistance to grain growth
answers.boundary_limitation: Detailed quantitative analysis of the 10 nm shift vs stability threshold not provided.
evidence_spans: Here, through a combined experimental and simulation methodology, we design a nanocrystalline refractory high entropy alloy (RHEA) system.
Compositions assessed under extreme environments and in situ electron-microscopy reveal both high thermal stability and radiation resistance.

We observe grain refinement under heavy ion irradiation and resistance to dual-beam irradiation and helium implantation in the form of low defect generation and evolution, as well as no detectable grain growth.

cross_paper_synthesis.consensus: There is a clear mechanistic consensus that in W-Ta-Cr-V-Hf RHEAs at high temperatures (1173 K), helium (He) implantation alone or in conjunction with thermal effects promotes a slight increase in grain size (approximately 10 nm), whereas the introduction of heavy ions in a dual-beam setup drives significant grain refinement and fragmentation.
cross_paper_synthesis.different_approaches: The papers approach the phenomenon by distinguishing the source of the driving force: Answer PMC10154406::reader_question::20f02e8a8f9c3642::answer::24737141e1662768 frames the 10 nm increase as a 'localized effect' of He implantation against the backdrop of thermal stability. In contrast, answers PMC10154406::reader_question::7711c954905654ab::answer::49180fa3570a2362 and PMC10154406::reader_question::da7fad08780db2e5::answer::130bff722be0f5f6 focus on the specific microstructural mechanism of the heavy ions, identifying 'overlapping cascades' as the agent of refinement.
cross_paper_synthesis.condition_dependencies: The outcome is strictly condition-dependent on the irradiation modality. He implantation alone leads to growth (PMC10154406::reader_question::20f02e8a8f9c3642::answer::24737141e1662768; PMC10154406::reader_question::7711c954905654ab::answer::49180fa3570a2362). The refinement only occurs when 'heavy ions are introduced' in a dual-beam configuration, creating a specific flux condition (PMC10154406::reader_question::da7fad08780db2e5::answer::130bff722be0f5f6).
cross_paper_synthesis.contradictions: No genuine contradictions exist. The observation of a 10 nm increase (PMC10154406::reader_question::20f02e8a8f9c3642::answer::24737141e1662768) is compatible with the observation of 'fragmentation' under dual-beam conditions because the fragmentation is explicitly attributed to the heavy ion component, not the He implantation. The He effect is described as a localized increase, while the heavy ion effect is a bulk refinement.
cross_paper_synthesis.evidence_strength: High. The consensus is supported by direct observation (PMC10154406::reader_question::20f02e8a8f9c3642::answer::24737141e1662768; PMC10154406::reader_question::7711c954905654ab::answer::49180fa3570a2362) and inference based on the real-time nature of in situ irradiation (PMC10154406::reader_question::da7fad08780db2e5::answer::130bff722be0f5f6).
cross_paper_synthesis.unresolved_gap: While the mechanisms are identified (thermal/He growth vs. cascade fragmentation), the specific quantitative threshold or 'stability threshold' where the competing forces balance is not detailed (PMC10154406::reader_question::20f02e8a8f9c3642::answer::24737141e1662768). Additionally, the exact beam parameters of the heavy ions beyond the general label are not specified (PMC10154406::reader_question::da7fad08780db2e5::answer::130bff722be0f5f6).
cross_paper_synthesis.candidate_hypothesis: Grain refinement in dual-beam irradiation is driven by the density of overlapping collision cascades exceeding the grain size, generating sufficient stacking faults to fragment grains, a process that overwhelms the thermally driven grain growth induced by helium implantation at 1173 K.
cross_paper_synthesis.discriminating_experiment: Perform sequential irradiation: first apply He implantation to induce the 10 nm growth, then introduce heavy ions to measure the rate of fragmentation relative to the initial grain size, specifically varying the heavy ion dose to identify the exact overlap density required to transition from stability to fragmentation.
